result:
The chart type gallery now shows on the insight page in view mode as well as edit mode, and the plain dropdown no longer takes its place there. Nothing was run, per your instructions: no tests, typecheck or lint, so this is unverified.

## What changed

The gallery was gated by a check in `chartAlternativesLogic` that required `editMode`. That check now accepts either edit mode or a new `insightPage` flag; every other condition is unchanged.

- **`InsightAsScene.tsx`** sets `insightPage: true` in the query context it passes down, so only the insight page opts in.
- **`frontend/src/queries/types.ts`** adds `insightPage` to `QueryContext`.
- **`InsightVizDisplay.tsx`** forwards `context?.insightPage` to `ChartAlternatives`.
- **`ChartAlternatives.tsx` / `ChartGallery.tsx`** accept the prop and pass it into the logic props.
- **`chartAlternativesLogic.ts`** adds the prop, a selector for it, and the widened check, with the inline kea types updated by hand to match.

## Behavior to be aware of

- **Other view-mode surfaces keep the dropdown.** Notebooks, dashboard cards, shared and embedded insights do not set the flag. I used an explicit flag because `query.full` is also set by web analytics, surveys and others.
- **Insights opened from a dashboard still get the dropdown**, in both modes. That exclusion already applied in edit mode and I left it alone.
- **The existing conditions still apply in view mode.** The gallery needs the `PRODUCT_ANALYTICS_CHART_ALTERNATIVES` flag, a trends query, and a user who can edit the insight; otherwise the dropdown shows.
- **Picking a chart in view mode changes the query the same way the dropdown did.** I did not touch how that change is saved.

## Test

I added one parameterized case to `ChartAlternatives.test.tsx` covering three surfaces:

| Surface | Expected control |
|---|---|
| Insight page, view mode | Gallery |
| View-mode chart outside the insight page | Dropdown |
| Shared insight page | Dropdown |

It guards against someone re-requiring edit mode, or the gallery leaking onto other view-mode surfaces.
